bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds: 50% to Phase 2 quartz, 20% to debt repayment, 30% to solar CAPEX; future HMS capex from internal accruals; no dividend policy disclosed; focus on deleveraging (debt/equity now 0.38x) and high-ROCE projects
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory delays in HMS licensing; monazite processing tech risk; global rare earth price volatility; execution risk on Phase 2 quartz commissioning; cyclone/flood disruptions to mining; KMLL MOU not yet signed
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, visionary, and execution-focused; repeatedly emphasized ‘world-class’ ambitions; strong emphasis on technology adoption (electric trucks, diamond wire R&D); transparent on one-offs; optimistic on rare earth tailwinds and import substitution
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Monazite from Sri Lanka is a low-cost byproduct of HMS mining — not a standalone cost center; KMLL LOI is a de facto off-take agreement for rare earth oxides; diamond wire manufacturing is a hidden margin enhancer used internally and sold externally; 99-day working capital is exceptional for mining sector
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "With strong leadership, a robust balance sheet, diversified reserves, and operational excellence" the company targets 35% ROCE alongside ₹300 crore of planned capex.
- "Strong track record of sustained growth, profitability and high quality earnings wherein receivables are backed by advances and letter of credits."
- Growth was "supported by a stringent credit policy and favorable customer payment terms that ensured healthy cash flow and reduced reliance on external financing".
- "CRISIL reaffirmed the Company's credit ratings at CRISIL A/Stable (Long Term) and CRISIL A1 (Short Term), reaffirming its strong credit profile."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- resource: Scarce Black Galaxy Granite resource where Midwest is the largest producer and exporter — evidence: commercially viable Black Galaxy deposits are concentrated in Andhra Pradesh (Chimakurthy); the Company accounted for approximately 64% (including third-party exports) of Black Galaxy Granite export volume during FY25; 8.47Mn CBM operational granite reserves — against it: a material share of natural-stone revenue derives from a limited number of product categories and export markets, with China an important destination
- cost position: Direct government lease on the new Black Galaxy mining area — evidence: the area adjoins existing operations allowing shared infrastructure, and the direct government lease offers lower consideration fees than the secondary sub-lease arrangements at existing operations; 10.9-hectare concession on a 20-year lease
- integration: In-house diamond wire manufacturing for precision cutting — evidence: the Diamond Wire division provides backward integration, supporting captive cutting efficiency and also serving external customers in mining, semiconductor and solar-processing segments
- resource: Captive quartz feedstock for the quartz-processing platform — evidence: 23Mt captive quartz resources; 30-year quarry lease for coloured quartzite with exclusive mining rights — against it: the coloured-quartzite B2B2C model remains at an early validation stage
- scale: Large quartz-processing facility — evidence: Quartz Phase I provides 303,600 TPA of installed capacity, described as India's largest quartz-processing facility — against it: monthly output reached only approximately 2,000 tonnes by April 2026 after stabilisation issues that created start-up costs of approximately H6 crore
- licence/regulatory: Monazite processing permission via the KMML rare-earth pilot — evidence: selected as Lead Consortium Partner by Kerala Minerals and Metals Limited for a rare-earth oxide pilot plant, becoming the first private company in India permitted to process monazite [planned] — against it: current rare-earth extraction recovery of approximately 87% compares with benchmark rates of 95 to 96%
- resource: Heavy mineral sands licences in Sri Lanka — evidence: 4 HMS exploration licences; identified resource base exceeds 3.5 million tonnes, an estimated 20 to 25 year operational runway [planned] — against it: the final mining licence remains pending and the licences remain subject to the evolving Sri Lankan policy framework
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export demand and construction-cycle sensitivity — The MD&A states natural-stone exports remain sensitive to construction demand, customer inventory cycles, freight availability, currency movements and changing trade conditions; export demand across international markets is uneven.
- Foreign-exchange exposure — The Company generates a material share of revenue from exports across 17 countries, so currency stability bears directly on natural-stone realisations and the competitiveness of its quartz and strategic-minerals verticals.
- Freight, energy and trade-restriction risk — Management names geopolitical tensions, energy prices, freight costs and trade restrictions as key risks in its global outlook; rising freight and logistics costs are listed as an industry challenge.
- Mining, environmental and operating approvals — Stringent mining, environmental and operating approvals are listed as a challenge for the granite and natural-stone business the Company depends on.
- Substitution by engineered surfaces — The MD&A flags increasing competition from engineered surfaces in selected applications as a challenge to natural-stone demand.
- Resource and product concentration in Black Galaxy Granite — The Company's position is built around Black Galaxy Granite, a variety the report says is found in only one location (Chimakurthy, Andhra Pradesh), tying the core business to a single product from a single geography.
- Dormant subsidiary under litigation — Subsidiary BEML Midwest Limited has had complete cessation of activities since September 2008 and its matters are subjudice before the NCLAT, so its financial statements could not be prepared.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "Over four decades of expertise in dimensional natural stone exploration, mining, processing, and global distribution across 17 countries and 5 continents, with key markets in China, Italy, and Thailand."
- "India's largest Black Galaxy Granite producer & exporter and largest Absolute Black Granite Producer"; the deck notes "Black Galaxy is available in only one village in Andhra Pradesh in the entire world".
- "Exclusive mining rights gives competitive edge in terms of strong revenue visibility" and the company "Serves as an organized player in an otherwise unorganized and fragmented market."
- Claims "India's largest integrated Quartz Processing Plant, supplying raw materials to solar glass and engineered stone manufacturers in domestic and export markets".
- Vision stated as "building leadership in quartz, titanium feedstock and rare earth oxides globally".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:

- [Market context] Deck cites CRISIL: "India currently imports 65% of its solar glass needs, but domestic supply is expected to rise to 70-80% by FY 2030" and "Quartz demand for solar glass is expected to grow at a CAGR of 30.7-31.4%, reaching 1,840-2,000 KT by FY 2030".

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Midwest Ltd., founded in 1981, mines and exports natural stone from Southern India, centred on Black Galaxy Granite and Absolute Black Granite, and operates an integrated mines-to-market model spanning exploration, extraction and in-house diamond wire manufacturing. It has commissioned a quartz-processing facility producing quartz grit and powder for engineered stone, solar glass and industrial customers, with a High-Purity Quartz line planned for semiconductor and solar crucibles. It is also developing heavy mineral sands (Sri Lanka licences) and rare-earth oxide processing (KMML pilot), while its Diamond Wire division serves captive cutting and external customers.

- **Heavy Mineral Sands and rare earths (emerging):** Ilmenite, rutile and zircon (planned Sri Lanka Phase I plant), Rare-earth oxides from monazite (KMML pilot)
- **Diamond Wire:** Diamond wire for precision cutting (captive and external customers)

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deliberate evolution from a predominantly natural stone business into an integrated materials enterprise spanning quartz/HPQ, heavy mineral sands and rare-earth oxides, funded by the cash flows of the granite business.
- Keep the granite core competitive: optimise resources, deepen customer relationships, improve operating efficiencies, develop new markets and keep securing quality resources (new 10.9-hectare Galaxy concession on a 20-year lease).
- Quartz: achieve consistent operating performance at Phase I while progressing Phase II, and fast-track High Purity Quartz product development within that phase to move up the value chain.
- Apply the integrated mine-to-market model to a fragmented, unorganised quartz grit and powder supply chain by combining captive resources, processing, quality control and reliable supply at scale.
- Heavy mineral sands: progress the Sri Lanka project from exploration towards mining, subject to regulatory approvals; Phase I intended to be funded through internal accruals after restructuring the proposed capital commitment.
- Rare earths: validate production of separated rare-earth oxides from crude monazite through the KMML pilot before any commercial development; MOU with PERMINAS, Indonesia to participate in rare-earth and critical minerals in Indonesia.
- Test a B2B2C model in coloured quartzite combining exclusive mineral access, external conversion partners and Midwest-controlled distribution.
- Electrify the mining fleet (electric dump trucks inducted, electric excavator prototype under testing) and expand captive solar to lower operating cost and carbon intensity.
- Fund each growth vertical through a matching capital structure, with disciplined capital allocation; jurisdiction, government commitments, investment structure and repatriation weigh on international investment decisions.
- Build organisational depth for a larger portfolio: specialist technical and leadership hiring, SAP HANA implementation, integrated HRMS and AI embedded in selected workflows.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Quartz Phase I was commissioned during FY26 and, after initial stabilisation issues, entered ramp-up (about 2,000 tonnes per month by April 2026), with management targeting 10,000-15,000 tonnes per month by end of Q1 FY27 and 60% utilisation in FY27. Quartz Phase II has moved into execution and is intended to double installed capacity to approximately 607,200 TPA, funded partly through IPO proceeds; the High-Purity Quartz line was advanced from Phase III into Phase II, with laboratory-scale work, raw-material identification and process-flow development completed. In granite, a new Black Galaxy mining area adjoining existing operations began production during the year, and a 30-year quarry lease for coloured quartzite was secured for an early-stage B2B2C model. In heavy mineral sands, Sri Lanka finalised its policy framework and Midwest has been asked to reconfirm its investment commitment, capacity and timelines; the final mining licence is pending, with a Phase I plant planned for 150,000 tonnes ROM feed producing ilmenite, rutile and zircon and commercial revenue conservatively expected from FY2029, Phase I to be funded through internal accruals. Midwest is Lead Consortium Partner for the KMML rare-earth pilot plant, on a six-month timeline commencing July 2026. IPO proceeds are also earmarked for electrification of the mining fleet.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic demand for natural stone is expected to remain a key support, driven by urbanisation, housing, hospitality and infrastructure expenditure; export demand may recover gradually.
- Black granite is expected to retain a differentiated position due to its limited geological availability and stronger value realisation versus commoditised stone.
- Natural-stone demand is shifting from volume-led raw-block exports towards value-added, customised products, while engineered surfaces compete in selected applications.
- Currency stability, freight-market normalisation and sustained trade flows matter directly because a material share of revenue comes from exports across 17 countries.
- Growth in solar manufacturing, semiconductors, electric mobility, aerospace and defence is expanding demand for processed quartz, High-Purity Quartz, titanium feedstocks and rare-earth elements.
- Highly concentrated high-purity quartz supply (a single US mine estimated at about 70% of natural HPQ) is raising buyer interest in alternative sources among solar-glass, crucible and wafer makers.
- A 34% decline in Indian raw-quartz exports during FY25 reinforces the shift towards domestic processing and value addition.
- Rare-earth supply concentration in China and 2025 export controls are accelerating investment in exploration, separation and refining outside established jurisdictions.
- HMS development in India is expected to proceed gradually given environmental, regulatory and technical requirements, with the strongest value creation in downstream separation and processing.
- Management expects blended returns to inch higher as the quartz and HMS verticals reach steady-state utilisation and the mix shifts toward higher-purity, higher-margin output.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Midwest has transformed from a granite miner to an integrated materials processor with Phase 1 quartz plant commissioned and Phase 2 + HMS facility funded by IPO proceeds, driving EBITDA margin expansion to 29% and positioning for 2.5x revenue growth by FY29 via rare earths and titanium feedstock — the key shift is from fragmented stone sales to high-margin, strategic raw material supply for solar, semiconductors, and defense.

The MD&A flags increasing competition from engineered surfaces in selected applications as a challenge to natural-stone demand.

The Company's position is built around Black Galaxy Granite, a variety the report says is found in only one location (Chimakurthy, Andhra Pradesh), tying the core business to a single product from a single geography.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Midwest Ltd., founded in 1981, mines and exports natural stone from Southern India, centred on Black Galaxy Granite and Absolute Black Granite, and operates an integrated mines-to-market model spanning exploration, extraction and in-house diamond wire manufacturing. It has commissioned a quartz-processing facility producing quartz grit and powder for engineered stone, solar glass and industrial customers, with a High-Purity Quartz line planned for semiconductor and solar crucibles. It is also developing heavy mineral sands (Sri Lanka licences) and rare-earth oxide processing (KMML pilot), while its Diamond Wire division serves captive cutting and external customers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic demand for natural stone is expected to remain a key support, driven by urbanisation, housing, hospitality and infrastructure expenditure; export demand may recover gradually.
- Black granite is expected to retain a differentiated position due to its limited geological availability and stronger value realisation versus commoditised stone.
- Natural-stone demand is shifting from volume-led raw-block exports towards value-added, customised products, while engineered surfaces compete in selected applications.
- Currency stability, freight-market normalisation and sustained trade flows matter directly because a material share of revenue comes from exports across 17 countries.
- Growth in solar manufacturing, semiconductors, electric mobility, aerospace and defence is expanding demand for processed quartz, High-Purity Quartz, titanium feedstocks and rare-earth elements.
- Highly concentrated high-purity quartz supply (a single US mine estimated at about 70% of natural HPQ) is raising buyer interest in alternative sources among solar-glass, crucible and wafer makers.
- A 34% decline in Indian raw-quartz exports during FY25 reinforces the shift towards domestic processing and value addition.
- Rare-earth supply concentration in China and 2025 export controls are accelerating investment in exploration, separation and refining outside established jurisdictions.
- HMS development in India is expected to proceed gradually given environmental, regulatory and technical requirements, with the strongest value creation in downstream separation and processing.
- Management expects blended returns to inch higher as the quartz and HMS verticals reach steady-state utilisation and the mix shifts toward higher-purity, higher-margin output.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds: 50% to Phase 2 quartz, 20% to debt repayment, 30% to solar CAPEX; future HMS capex from internal accruals; no dividend policy disclosed; focus on deleveraging (debt/equity now 0.38x) and high-ROCE projects

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Quartz Phase I was commissioned during FY26 and, after initial stabilisation issues, entered ramp-up (about 2,000 tonnes per month by April 2026), with management targeting 10,000-15,000 tonnes per month by end of Q1 FY27 and 60% utilisation in FY27. Quartz Phase II has moved into execution and is intended to double installed capacity to approximately 607,200 TPA, funded partly through IPO proceeds; the High-Purity Quartz line was advanced from Phase III into Phase II, with laboratory-scale work, raw-material identification and process-flow development completed. In granite, a new Black Galaxy mining area adjoining existing operations began production during the year, and a 30-year quarry lease for coloured quartzite was secured for an early-stage B2B2C model. In heavy mineral sands, Sri Lanka finalised its policy framework and Midwest has been asked to reconfirm its investment commitment, capacity and timelines; the final mining licence is pending, with a Phase I plant planned for 150,000 tonnes ROM feed producing ilmenite, rutile and zircon and commercial revenue conservatively expected from FY2029, Phase I to be funded through internal accruals. Midwest is Lead Consortium Partner for the KMML rare-earth pilot plant, on a six-month timeline commencing July 2026. IPO proceeds are also earmarked for electrification of the mining fleet.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- resource: Scarce Black Galaxy Granite resource where Midwest is the largest producer and exporter — evidence: commercially viable Black Galaxy deposits are concentrated in Andhra Pradesh (Chimakurthy); the Company accounted for approximately 64% (including third-party exports) of Black Galaxy Granite export volume during FY25; 8.47Mn CBM operational granite reserves — against it: a material share of natural-stone revenue derives from a limited number of product categories and export markets, with China an important destination
- cost position: Direct government lease on the new Black Galaxy mining area — evidence: the area adjoins existing operations allowing shared infrastructure, and the direct government lease offers lower consideration fees than the secondary sub-lease arrangements at existing operations; 10.9-hectare concession on a 20-year lease
- integration: In-house diamond wire manufacturing for precision cutting — evidence: the Diamond Wire division provides backward integration, supporting captive cutting efficiency and also serving external customers in mining, semiconductor and solar-processing segments
- resource: Captive quartz feedstock for the quartz-processing platform — evidence: 23Mt captive quartz resources; 30-year quarry lease for coloured quartzite with exclusive mining rights — against it: the coloured-quartzite B2B2C model remains at an early validation stage
- scale: Large quartz-processing facility — evidence: Quartz Phase I provides 303,600 TPA of installed capacity, described as India's largest quartz-processing facility — against it: monthly output reached only approximately 2,000 tonnes by April 2026 after stabilisation issues that created start-up costs of approximately H6 crore
- licence/regulatory: Monazite processing permission via the KMML rare-earth pilot — evidence: selected as Lead Consortium Partner by Kerala Minerals and Metals Limited for a rare-earth oxide pilot plant, becoming the first private company in India permitted to process monazite [planned] — against it: current rare-earth extraction recovery of approximately 87% compares with benchmark rates of 95 to 96%
- resource: Heavy mineral sands licences in Sri Lanka — evidence: 4 HMS exploration licences; identified resource base exceeds 3.5 million tonnes, an estimated 20 to 25 year operational runway [planned] — against it: the final mining licence remains pending and the licences remain subject to the evolving Sri Lankan policy framework

risks.body: Regulatory delays in HMS licensing; monazite processing tech risk; global rare earth price volatility; execution risk on Phase 2 quartz commissioning; cyclone/flood disruptions to mining; KMLL MOU not yet signed

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Monazite from Sri Lanka is a low-cost byproduct of HMS mining — not a standalone cost center; KMLL LOI is a de facto off-take agreement for rare earth oxides; diamond wire manufacturing is a hidden margin enhancer used internally and sold externally; 99-day working capital is exceptional for mining sector
